newsitem.title: USA: Chevron expects US Gulf gas, crude cuts back Tues.
newsitem.headline: Chevron expects US Gulf gas, crude cuts back Tues.

text.p: Chevron Corp said Tuesday that it expected U.S. Gulf natural gas and crude oil production shut this week as a precaution against Tropical Storm Josephine to be fully restored by the end of the day.
"We're in good shape. We're staging our people back. Part of our production has been restored and we expect to be fully back by the end of the day," a company spokeswoman said.
She declined to estimate the amount of crude oil and gas shut in as platforms were evacuated ahead of the storm.
A year ago, Chevron was producing about 1.2 billion cubic feet per day of gas and 125,000 to 130,000 barrels per day of crude in the U.S. Gulf.

Josephine was downgraded overnight from a tropical storm, as it dissipated when it moved across Florida. At 0500 EDT, the storm was located 50 miles southeast of Savannah, Georgia, moving east-northeast at 25 mph, with winds of about 50 mph.
